title: _admissible treats max_rank_increase=0 as zero increase, not RFC unlimited
description:
## Location

python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py DodagState._admissible (lines 244-250).

RFC 6550 Section 6.7.6 MaxRankIncrease: "If this is set to 0, then there is no limit." rust/lichen-rpl candidate_admissible implements that with `max_rank_increase == 0 || lowest_rank == INFINITE_RANK || cost <= lowest.saturating_add(max_rank_increase)`.

## What goes wrong

Python:

    if self._lowest_rank >= INFINITE_RANK:
        return True
    return cost <= self._lowest_rank + self.max_rank_increase

When max_rank_increase is 0 and _lowest_rank is finite, this is `cost <= _lowest_rank`: any worse (or even slightly worse after parent loss) candidate is inadmissible. That is the opposite of the RFC meaning of 0.

Trigger:
1. DodagState(..., max_rank_increase=0) — RFC default / a caller copying DEFAULT_MAX_RANK_INCREASE=0.
2. Node joins via P1, rank 512, _lowest_rank=512.
3. P1 fails. Backup P2 would cost 768 (still a valid local-repair parent).
4. _admissible rejects P2; select_parent unjoins. The node has no route instead of failing over.

After demote(), _lowest_rank is INFINITE so the first rejoin still works; the bound only bites once a finite lowest rank is recorded. Dual-impl: the same max_rank_increase=0 on the Rust side allows the failover (test zero_max_rank_increase_disables_the_bound).

## Fix

Treat max_rank_increase == 0 as unlimited, matching RFC 6550 6.7.6 and rust/lichen-rpl. Keep the existing finite-bound path for the LICHEN default (2048).
close_reason: _admissible: max_rank_increase==0 is unlimited per RFC 6550 6.7.6. test_max_rank_increase_zero_is_unlimited.
